headline: Capcom plans to turn its RE Engine into an AI-assisted game engine without putting AI-made assets in its games.
score_reason: Kept at 5: a clear plan from a major publisher, but the conference was on 2 Oct 2026 and it is a roadmap rather than a shipped product.
importance_line: Game developers at one of Japan's biggest studios will see AI built into their daily tools, players are promised no AI-generated art, and the honest doubt is that the plan is gradual and the line between helper and generator may blur.
summary: IGN reports, citing the Japanese outlet GameBiz, that at its Capcom Open Conference RE: 2026 on 2 Oct 2026 programmer Satoshi Ishida laid out the REX project, a step-by-step upgrade of the Resident Evil maker's RE Engine aimed at making it an AI-generation game engine where staff "create games together with AI". Capcom says the aim is to speed up development of very large games, and it told shareholders in March 2026 that it will not put AI-generated assets into its games.
notes: Pool item was The Verge (https://www.theverge.com/games/1004418/capcom-ai-game-development), which rests on IGN; IGN rests on GameBiz, so source is IGN, citing GameBiz. Event one day before the window; score not lowered for a one-day lag.
